userStories.title: Add clamp function to src/math.ts as a named export
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a `clamp(value, min, max)` function to `src/math.ts`, next to `add`, exported as a named export, leaving `add` and `negate` unchanged.

**Motivation** — The spec requires a clamp helper that limits a value to the inclusive range `[min, max]` and throws when `min > max`.

**Approach** — Implement `clamp` in `src/math.ts` as a named export alongside `add` and `negate`, with tests added to the existing `test/math.test.ts` (one `bun:test` file per module; do not create a new test file). Behavior:
- Return `value` when `min <= value <= max` (e.g. `clamp(5, 0, 10)` → `5`).
- Return `min` when `value < min` (e.g. `clamp(-3, 0, 10)` → `0`).
- Return `max` when `value > max` (e.g. `clamp(42, 0, 10)` → `10`).
- Throw `new Error('min must not exceed max')` when `min > max`; the `min > max` check must execute BEFORE any clamping logic so `clamp(1, 5, 2)` throws even though its value is not within a valid range.
- `add` and `negate` are not modified in any way — same signatures, same behavior.
- Spec AC5 requires that `bun test` and `bun run typecheck` pass after the change; both are run by the pipeline.

**Scope** — In: `src/math.ts` (add `clamp` export), `test/math.test.ts` (clamp coverage under a new `describe('clamp')` block). Out: any other math functions, new files outside `src/` and `test/`, and any change under `.github/` — plus any change to `add`/`negate`.

**Interface**
```typescript
export function clamp(value: number, min: number, max: number): number
```
acceptanceCriteria: clamp(1, 5, 2) throws Error with message 'min must not exceed max'
bun test and bun run typecheck pass
add(2, 3) returns 5 and negate(5) returns -5 after clamp is added — add and negate are unchanged

routing.reasoning: Single purely additive function in one existing source file plus its test block in the existing module test file; standard patterns, no new dependencies, no state or concurrency, no security implications — lightest realistic routing.

suggestedCriteria: clamp(0, 0, 10) returns 0 and clamp(10, 0, 10) returns 10 (range boundaries are inclusive)
clamp(7, 5, 5) returns 5 and clamp(3, 5, 5) returns 5 when min equals max
clamp(-100, 5, 2) throws Error with message 'min must not exceed max' — the min > max check wins even when value is below both bounds
outOfScope: Any other math functions, new files outside `src/` and `test/`, and any change under `.github/`.

analysis: Tiny, pure TypeScript library (Bun + strict TS, named exports only, one bun:test file per module). Existing files: src/math.ts (8 lines) exports add and negate; test/math.test.ts (26 lines) covers add and negate (incl. canonical zero via Object.is). No other src files, no consumers outside the repo (greenfield library surface). The feature adds clamp(value, min, max): number as a third named export in src/math.ts next to add. Impact is confined to src/math.ts (modified) and test/math.test.ts (modified — existing module test file, per the 'one test file per module' convention; no new test file needed). No other files import math.ts, so no downstream breakage risk. Backward compatibility: add and negate are untouched; clamp is purely additive — guard this with a regression assertion since the spec marks it as 'unchanged'. Implementation decisions: error check `if (min > max) throw new Error('min must not exceed max')` must run BEFORE clamping so clamp(1, 5, 2) throws regardless of value; return Math.max(min, Math.min(max, value)) or equivalent three-branch logic; inclusive bounds ([min, max]). The spec's AC5 ('bun test and bun run typecheck pass') is preserved as an acceptance criterion; the test and typecheck stages also run automatically in the pipeline. Test cases should live in test/math.test.ts under a new describe('clamp', ...) block with one test per AC; suggested hardening: inclusive boundaries, equal min===max, floating point, negative values below both bounds when min>max (error still wins).
outOfScope: Any other math functions, new files outside `src/` and `test/`, and any change under `.github/`.
